# TESS Program G09102

Title: Survivors Of Stellar Evolution: A TESS Survey For Eclipsing Companions Of White Dwarfs

PI: Rackham, Benjamin - Massachusetts Institute Of Technology

Type: LARGE

Summary: White dwarfs provide a unique opportunity to detect close companions that have survived stellar evolution. Because white dwarfs are Earth-sized, even small companions can produce deep, short eclipses detectable in high-cadence photometry. We propose a systematic search for eclipsing companions among 12,967 white dwarfs observable during TESS Cycle 9 using 120-second cadence observations. A pilot analysis of archival TESS data identified 180 candidate eclipse signals among 5,800 white dwarfs, demonstrating the effectiveness of our detection pipeline. We will publish a catalog of all detected signals and pursue ground-based follow-up for a subset of exciting candidates. This program will expand the known population of compact white dwarf binaries and constrain common-envelope evolution.
